title: Lincoln's Niagara speech on the giants whose bones fill the mounds
summary: Tim Alberino tells of Lincoln's Niagara speech on the giants whose bones fill the mounds, about 19th century at United States (no place named), and summarises it without a named source. As told, not a fact.

tellings.quote: Abraham Lincoln who's waxing poetically about Niagara Falls in a speech in which he says, "The eyes of that ancient species of giants whose bones fill the mounds of America have gazed upon Niagara as ours do."

plain: A researcher, Tim Alberino, points to a speech about Niagara Falls written by Abraham Lincoln, the American president. He quotes Lincoln as saying that "that ancient species of giants whose bones fill the mounds of America" once gazed on Niagara as we do now, meaning the old earth mounds found across the country. Alberino offers it as a sign that giants were once openly talked about in America.
